target: Ela deu com a língua nos dentes.
english: She let the cat out of the bag.
tip: Dar com a língua nos dentes is literally your tongue hitting your teeth, the moment a secret slips out and gets told.

target: A pessoa a quem me refiro não está presente.
english: The person I'm referring to is not present.
tip: Portuguese can't leave a preposition dangling at the end like English does. Referir-se keeps its a up front: a quem me refiro.

target: O fato de ele ter se atrasado comprometeu toda a programação.
english: The fact that he was late compromised the entire schedule.
tip: Where English says the fact that he was late, Portuguese uses an infinitive with its own subject: o fato de ele ter se atrasado.

target: A cidade que outrora fora próspera agora jazia em ruínas.
english: The city that had once been prosperous now lay in ruins.
tip: Fora próspera means had been prosperous. This -ra pluperfect is literary; in speech you'd say tinha sido próspera instead.

target: A verdade é que, por mais que tentemos, erros acontecem.
english: The truth is that, no matter how hard we try, mistakes happen.
tip: 'Por mais que' + subjunctive means 'no matter how much' – expresses concession.

target: Se vocês quiserem, podemos remarcar.
english: If you want, we can reschedule.
tip: After se for a future possibility, Portuguese uses the future subjunctive quiserem, while English just keeps the plain present want.

target: Quem quiser participar, que se inscreva.
english: Whoever wants to participate should register.
tip: Que plus a subjunctive is a third-person command or wish: que se inscreva means let them register, or they should register.

target: Em que pese a oposição, o projeto seguiu adiante.
english: Notwithstanding the opposition, the project moved forward.
tip: Pese comes from pesar, to weigh, so em que pese is roughly however it may weigh, a frozen formal formula meaning despite.

target: A empresa, cujo faturamento triplicou, planeja expandir.
english: The company, whose revenue tripled, plans to expand.
tip: Cujo means whose and agrees with the thing owned, not the owner: cujo is masculine here because faturamento is masculine.

target: Herdara do pai o gosto pela música.
english: He had inherited his father's love of music.
tip: Herdara is the simple pluperfect: one word for had inherited. The -ara ending marks it, and it is mostly literary now.

target: A questão à qual me refiro é de ordem ética.
english: The issue I'm referring to is of an ethical nature.
tip: Refiro needs the preposition a (referir-se a), so the relative takes it too, and a plus a qual contracts to à qual.

target: Quanto mais se analisa, mais complexo o problema parece.
english: The more you analyze it, the more complex the problem seems.
tip: 'Quanto mais...mais' is the Portuguese equivalent of 'the more...the more' – a correlative structure.

target: O barato sai caro.
english: Cheap things end up costing more.
tip: Put o before an adjective to turn it into a noun: o barato means the cheap thing or option.

target: Aquela experiência marcara-o profundamente.
english: That experience had marked him deeply.
tip: Marcara is the simple pluperfect, a one-word literary form equal to tinha marcado (had marked). Rare in speech, common in writing.

target: Se a chuva parar, saímos.
english: If the rain stops, we'll go out.
tip: Se (if) about the future uses the future subjunctive: se a chuva parar. For regular verbs the form looks identical to the infinitive.

target: Jamais vira paisagem tão deslumbrante.
english: He had never seen such a stunning landscape.
tip: Vira here is the pluperfect of ver (had seen), a one-word had-form. Do not confuse it with virar, meaning to turn.

target: Quando você trouxer os documentos, poderemos prosseguir.
english: When you bring the documents, we can proceed.
tip: Trouxer is the future subjunctive of trazer (to bring); its stem comes from the preterite trouxe, not the infinitive.

target: Se eu obtiver a aprovação, começo na semana que vem.
english: If I get approval, I start next week.
tip: After se for a future condition, Portuguese uses the future subjunctive: Se eu obtiver a aprovação means if I get approval.

target: Cumpre salientar que a amostra é limitada.
english: It should be noted that the sample is limited.
tip: Cumpre plus an infinitive is an impersonal formal phrase: cumpre salientar means it should be pointed out.

target: Depreende-se, pois, que o fenômeno é multifacetado.
english: It can therefore be inferred that the phenomenon is multifaceted.
tip: Set off by commas mid-sentence, pois means therefore, not because. It is a formal connector in academic writing.

target: Em boca fechada não entra mosca.
english: In a closed mouth, no flies enter.
tip: Boca fechada, a closed mouth, carries the lesson: keep quiet, no flies get in, and you stay out of trouble.

target: Faz-se mister uma abordagem interdisciplinar.
english: An interdisciplinary approach is required.
tip: In faz-se mister, mister means necessary and has nothing to do with the English title. It's archaic formal speak for it is required.

target: Uma andorinha só não faz verão.
english: One swallow doesn't make a summer.
tip: Here só means alone or by itself, not only: uma andorinha só is one swallow on its own.

target: Quem não cola não sai da escola.
english: Those who don't cheat don't make it through school.
tip: Cola comes from colar, literally to glue, but in school slang it means to cheat; a cola is a crib sheet.

target: Quem espera sempre alcança.
english: Good things come to those who wait.
tip: Quem as whoever takes a third-person singular verb: quem espera alcança, never quem esperam.

target: Quem com os porcos se mistura, farelo come.
english: Whoever associates with pigs will eat bran.
tip: Mix with the porcos and you'll end up eating farelo, bran: the proverb warns that bad company rubs off on you.

target: No que tange à metodologia, adotou-se uma abordagem qualitativa.
english: Regarding methodology, a qualitative approach was adopted.
tip: à merges the preposition a with the feminine article a before a feminine noun: tange à metodologia (regarding the methodology).

target: Infere-se que as políticas públicas são insuficientes.
english: It is inferred that public policies are insufficient.
tip: Infere-se puts se on the verb with no stated subject: it is inferred or one infers. Standard in formal writing.

target: Malgrado as limitações, o estudo traz contribuições relevantes.
english: Despite the limitations, the study makes relevant contributions.
tip: Malgrado means despite and attaches straight to a noun, with no de: malgrado as limitações (despite the limitations).

target: O presente estudo visa analisar os impactos da urbanização.
english: This study aims to analyze the impacts of urbanization.
tip: 'Visa analisar' or 'visa a analisar' – both are accepted in academic writing.
